output.best_reason: Version D has the most distinct voice. Vauthier is witty and self-aware ("Aurèle was always kinder to his friends' watches than to their opinions"; "a physician who guesses at the rest is worth less than a clerk"). The subtext works: Madame "did not look up," and the closing "Nor, I think, is anyone" builds tension. The facts come up through conversation rather than a list. Its weak point is the mallet, which sits a little too conveniently in the physician's mouth. Version A is close behind, with a tight rhythm, a crisp refusal on the time of death ("A man struck down is not a clock"), and a well-placed watch motif. Version C has good period texture and emotional weight, but it leans sentimental ("I am a foolish old man"). Version B is the most conventional: its opening grief speech slows the start, and its answers are flatter.
